language.script_notes: Chinese and Korean shop signage turns up in Vladivostok and near the border crossings.

road_furniture.guardrail_type: Steel W-beam on the main routes; hilly coastal roads with drops.
road_furniture.line_paint: Centre lines in the cities and on the Vladivostok–Khabarovsk highway; unmarked elsewhere.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: White sign poles with a black base band. Vladivostok has steep, cable-strung hillside streets.

architecture.roof_style: Flat Soviet block roofs; pitched roofs on wooden houses inland.
architecture.wall_construction: Soviet panel blocks in the cities, some climbing steep hillsides in Vladivostok; timber houses in the interior and on Sakhalin.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Grey concrete, faded paint; occasional Chinese-influenced signage colours near the border.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Vladivostok's hilly, bridge-spanned, faintly San-Francisco-like cityscape; standard panelki; wooden villages inland; Japanese-era buildings on southern Sakhalin.

nature.vegetation: Manchurian mixed forest — Korean pine, oak, maple, lianas — more diverse than Siberian taiga, with a monsoon-green look in summer; birch and larch inland and to the north.
nature.terrain: Hilly and mountainous (the Sikhote-Alin range) with a deeply indented Pacific coast, the long island of Sakhalin, and the volcanoes of Kamchatka further north.
nature.climate_signature: Monsoon-influenced — humid, often foggy summers and cold, dry, snowy winters. Greener and mistier than inland Siberia.

vehicles.plate_color: White with a region number — 25/125 Primorsky Krai, 27 Khabarovsk, 65 Sakhalin, 41 Kamchatka.
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: The signature Far East tell: huge numbers of imported second-hand Japanese cars with the steering wheel on the RIGHT, driven on right-hand roads. Toyota, Nissan and Honda dominate; almost no Ladas by comparison.

google_coverage.coverage_notes: Concentrated around Vladivostok, Khabarovsk, Sakhalin and the highway between them, with big gaps. Often overcast or foggy on the coast.

confusion_set.shared_traits: The same Manchurian forest, hills and climate run straight across the border; Chinese signage appears on the Russian side too
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Russian Cyrillic and region-number plates vs Chinese Hanzi and plates; China's official Street View is minimal, so extensive coverage of this landscape is the Russian side.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Same country — Cyrillic, panelki, Russian plates, taiga inland
confusion_set.tiebreaker: The Far East has right-hand-drive Japanese cars driven on the right, hilly Pacific coastline and more diverse Manchurian forest; Siberia is flatter taiga with mostly left-hand-drive Ladas and the railway corridor.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Right-hand-drive Japanese cars, hilly coast, misty maritime climate
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Japan drives on the LEFT and uses kana/kanji; the Far East drives on the RIGHT with Cyrillic signage and Soviet panel blocks.
